WCAG 2.2 · SC 2.3.3 ANIMATION FROM INTERACTIONS · LEVEL AAA

Motion review checklist

SC 2.3.3: motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information being conveyed. Whether motion can be turned off is not visible in pixels, so this is a structured manual review. No conformance verdict is produced.

How to test each interaction
  1. List every interaction that starts motion: scrolling (parallax, scroll-linked effects, reveal-on-scroll), hover and focus effects, clicks that slide, zoom, spin or move content, page and route transitions, carousels you advance, drag effects.
  2. Trigger it with no motion preference set and note the motion.
  3. Turn on reduced motion and repeat: macOS System Settings → Accessibility → Display → Reduce motion; Windows Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects off; or Chrome DevTools → Rendering → Emulate CSS prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
  4. Also look for a site setting that turns animation off, and check that it persists across pages.
  5. If motion is not disabled, decide whether it is essential (the function or information would be lost without it) and write down why.
  6. Motion that is not triggered by an interaction (autoplay) falls under SC 2.2.2. Flashing falls under SC 2.3.1 and SC 2.3.2: use the capture tool or file analysis for those.
